Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Who among these four was born earliest?
Thomas Carlyle (born 1795) is the earliest of the four. Thomas Carlyle (4 December 1795 – 5 February 1881) was a Scottish essayist, historian and philosopher.
Which of these was founded earliest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below is best known as an astronomer?
Arthur Eddington is an astronomer. Sir Arthur Stanley Eddington (28 December 1882 – 22 November 1944) was an English astrophysicist and mathematician.
Which one below is best known as a mathematician?
Archimedes is a mathematician. Archimedes died during the siege of Syracuse, when he was killed by a Roman soldier despite orders that he should not be harmed.
What is the atomic number of Radium?
Radium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ra and atomic number 88.
What is the atomic number of Zinc?
Zinc is a chemical element; it has symbol Zn and atomic number 30.
In what year did Stephen Hawking die?
Stephen Hawking: Hawking was born in Oxford into a family of physicians.
In what year was Theobroma cacao discovered?
Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Mikoyan MiG-31: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-31 is the fastest known operational combat aircraft, with a top speed around 3,000 km/h (1,600 knots).
Which company manufactures CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder?
CAC/PAC JF-17 Thunder: Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group. The JF-17 can be used for multiple roles, including interception, ground attack, anti-ship, and aerial reconnaissance.
Who is credited with discovering Triangulum Australe?
Triangulum Australe: Américo Vespucio. Triangulum Australe is a small constellation in the far Southern Celestial Hemisphere.
Who is credited with discovering Ichthyosaurus?
Ichthyosaurus: Mary Anning. It is among the best known ichthyosaur genera, as it is the type genus of the order Ichthyosauria.
Who is credited with discovering Theobroma cacao?
Theobroma cacao: Christopher Columbus. Theobroma cacao (cacao tree or cocoa tree) is a small (6–12 m (20–39 ft) tall) evergreen tree in the Malvaceae family.
Who is credited with discovering Krypton?
Krypton: William Ramsay. Krypton (from Ancient Greek: κρυπτός, romanized: kryptos 'the hidden one') is a chemical element; it has symbol Kr and atomic number 36.

First coined as a term in 1852, this pattern of continued drinking despite its harms affected an estimated 283 million people worldwide as of 2016, according to the World Health Organization — name the condition?
Alcoholism is the continued drinking of alcohol despite the problems it causes.
This order of ray-finned fish is named for a modified fin ray that dangles like bait to lure in prey, much like a human with a fishing rod — what are they called?

Anglerfish are ray-finned fish in the order Lophiiformes. The majority are bottom-dwellers, being demersal fish, while the aberrant deep-sea anglerfish are pelagic, (mostly) living high in the water column.

This English science fiction writer, futurist, and undersea explorer received the 1961 Kalinga Prize, a UNESCO award for popularizing science, across a career spanning novels, essays, and television hosting — who is he?
Arthur C. Clarke (16 December 1917 - 19 March 2008) was an English science fiction writer, science writer, futurist, inventor, undersea explorer, and television series host.
Coming on over about 48 hours, this temporary one-sided facial paralysis of unknown cause can droop an eyebrow, alter taste, and make sounds painfully loud — what is it?
Bell's palsy is a type of facial paralysis that results in a temporary inability to control the facial muscles on the affected side of the face.
Element 107, a synthetic transactinide whose most stable known isotope lasts barely 2.4 minutes, takes its name from a famous Danish physicist — what is it?
Bohrium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Bh and atomic number 107.
Unlike ordinary weight loss from undereating, this illness-linked syndrome strips away muscle mass in ways good nutrition can't fully undo — what condition is it?
Cachexia is a syndrome that occurs in people with certain illnesses, causing muscle loss that cannot be fully reversed with improved nutrition.

Derived from the amino acid tyrosine and fifty percent bound to plasma proteins in your bloodstream, what class of neurotransmitter has a benzene ring topped with two hydroxyl groups plus a side-chain amine?

Catecholamine (abbreviated CA), most typically a 3,4-dihydroxyphenethylamine, is a monoamine neurotransmitter, an organic compound that has a catechol (benzene with two hydroxyl side groups next to each other) and a side-chain amine.
Grown for blue-flowered roadside roots that become a coffee substitute, or for bitter salad leaves like escarole and radicchio, which plant genus covers both chicory and endive?
Cichorium is a genus of plants in the tribe Cichorieae within the family Asteraceae.
This common bowel condition causes hard, dry stools passed fewer than three times a week, sometimes leading to hemorrhoids or fissures — what is it?
Constipation is a bowel dysfunction that makes bowel movements infrequent or hard to pass.
This Canadian-born entrepreneur co-founded a company later acquired by MSC Software in 1998, then went on to co-found and lead a massively popular online gaming and creation platform — who is he?
David Baszucki (buh-; born January 20, 1963) is a Canadian-born American entrepreneur, engineer, and software developer.
First proposed as a model organism in 1901, this tiny insect species has become biology's workhorse for genetics research, and it's the one buzzing around your rotting fruit bowl. Name the species?
Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fly (an insect of the order Diptera) in the family Drosophilidae.
Practitioners of this zoological discipline have identified more than 1.3 million species within a single group of arthropods — what is it called?
Entomology (ntomon), meaning "insect", and (lgos), meaning "study", is the branch of zoology that focuses on insects.

This synthetic opioid is 50 to 100 times more potent than morphine and is now notorious in emergency medicine. Initially developed as a pain medication for cancer patients and post-surgical recovery, it works by activating opioid receptors — what is this drug?
Fentanyl is a highly potent synthetic opioid of the piperidine family, used primarily as pain medication.

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'milky,' this term names any gravity-bound system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter, ranging from tiny dwarfs to supergiants with a hundred trillion stars. What is it?
Galaxy is a system of stars, stellar remnants, interstellar gas, dust, and dark matter bound together by gravity.
This large, semi-bitter citrus fruit originated in Barbados as an accidental 18th-century hybrid of the sweet orange and the pomelo, and has also been called the 'forbidden fruit.' What is it?
Grapefruit (Citrus paradisi) is a subtropical citrus tree known for its relatively large, sour to semi-sweet, somewhat bitter fruit.

Known as 'The Last Universalist' for mastering nearly every branch of his field, this French mathematician and physicist founded modern chaos theory through his study of the three-body problem — who is he?
Henri Poincaré (29 April 1854 - 17 July 1912) was a French mathematician, theoretical physicist, engineer, and philosopher of science.
A body-temperature emergency defined as a reading above 104°F, this condition kills roughly half a million people annually and is most commonly triggered by heat stroke — what is it called?
Hyperthermia is a condition in which an individual's body temperature is elevated beyond normal due to failed thermoregulation.

From deep-sea gribbles to the woodlice under your garden stones, members of this crustacean order share seven pairs of jointed limbs and brood their young in a pouch called a marsupium — what is the order?
Isopoda is an order of crustaceans. The order is divided into eleven suborders.

After leaving the company where he led industrial design for decades, this British-American designer founded the creative collective LoveFrom, which now works with Ferrari, Airbnb, and OpenAI. Who is he?
Jony Ive (born 27 February 1967) is a British-American designer.
This genus of deciduous conifers, unusual for shedding its needles each year, dominates the boreal forests of Siberia and Canada, making it the most abundant tree genus on Earth — what is it called?
Larch are deciduous conifers in the genus Larix, of the family Pinaceae.
Only about 35 atoms of this synthetic element (symbol Lv, number 116) had ever been made as of 2020 — named for a California national laboratory. Which element is it?
Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
Sometimes nicknamed 'sea cows,' these large, fully aquatic herbivorous marine mammals can grow up to 13 feet long and include Amazonian, West Indian, and West African species — what are they called?
Manatee (family Trichechidae, genus Trichechus) are large, fully aquatic, mostly herbivorous marine mammals sometimes known as sea cows.
Its three main jobs are converting food into usable energy, building macromolecules like proteins and lipids, and excreting waste — the chemistry that keeps every living thing alive. What is it?
Metabolism (from) refers to the set of life-sustaining chemical reactions that occur within living organisms.
Named for the river near which its type fossil was found by a Dutch chalk quarry in the 18th century, this genus of marine reptile lived until the end of the Cretaceous — what is it?
Mosasaurus ("lizard of the Meuse River") is the type genus (defining example) of the Mosasauridae, an extinct group of aquatic squamate reptiles.
Named for a pioneering physicist's work on classical mechanics, this SI unit of force equals the push needed to accelerate one kilogram at one metre per second squared — name the unit?
Newton (unit) (symbol: N) is the unit of force in the International System of Units (SI).

These pouched mammals originated in South America and crossed into the north during the Great American Interchange; one species is so common in the U.S. that people just call it a 'possum.' What is it?
Opossum are members of the marsupial order Didelphimorphia endemic to the Americas.
This New York Times columnist of 24 years was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel in economics for explaining the patterns of international trade and where economic activity clusters. Who is he?
Paul Krugman (born February 28, 1953) is an American economist who is the Distinguished Professor of Economics at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York.
Odorless when pure but reeking of rotting fish in technical grade, this colorless PH3 gas can burst into a luminous flame on contact with air — what highly toxic compound is it?
Phosphine (IUPAC name: phosphane) is a colorless, flammable, highly toxic compound with the chemical formula PH3, classed as a pnictogen hydride.
Though it looks like a small dolphin, this cetacean is actually more closely related to narwhals and belugas, and can be told apart by its flattened, spade-shaped teeth — what animal is it?
Porpoise are small dolphin-like cetaceans classified under the family Phocoenidae.
Its blossoms are a beloved symbol of early spring throughout East Asia, and its crunchy fruit is marketed globally as the Asian or nashi pear - which tree species?
Pyrus pyrifolia is a species of pear tree native to southern China and northern Indochina that has been introduced to Korea, Japan and other parts of the world.

A brilliant English anatomist who coined the word 'Dinosauria,' meaning roughly 'terrible reptile,' he accepted that evolution happened but was an outspoken critic of Darwin's account of it. Who was he?
Richard Owen (20 July 1804 - 18 December 1892) was an English biologist, comparative anatomist and palaeontologist.
Marked by hearing voices, disorganized thinking, and flat affect, this condition is diagnosed by observed behavior rather than any objective test — what is it?
Schizophrenia is a mental disorder characterized variously by hallucinations (typically, hearing voices), delusions, disorganized thinking or behavior, and flat or inappropriate affect.
Long, thin and transparent, this hydrozoan drifts through the ocean as a colony of specialized zooids that together handle feeding, floating and jet propulsion — what marine organism is this?
Siphonophore (from Ancient Greek (siphn), meaning "tube" and - (-phros), meaning "bearing") are cnidarian animals of the hydrozoan order Siphonophorae.

Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes' and 'kernel,' this genus of spherical, Gram-positive bacteria grows in grape-like clusters and can survive with or without oxygen — what's the genus called?
Staphylococcus (staphul), meaning "bunch of grapes", and (kkkos), meaning "kernel" or "Kermes", is a genus of Gram-positive bacteria in the family Staphylococcaceae from the order Bacillales.
Though some scientists place it in its own genus, Acrocodia, the Malayan species is usually still classified within this genus of tapir — name this genus?
Tapirus is a genus of tapir which contains the living tapir species.
This intensely itchy, contagious fungal skin infection produces a red, scaly rash with a curved border across the groin and buttocks, mostly in men — what is it?

Tinea cruris (TC), also known as jock itch, is a common type of contagious, superficial fungal infection of the groin and buttocks region, which occurs predominantly but not exclusively in men and in hot-humid climates.
This bodily fluid, produced by the kidneys to flush out urea and other waste, can also serve a second life as a nitrogen-rich fertilizer for soil — what is it?
Urine is the fluid excreted by the kidneys of vertebrates to clear the bloodstream of excess water and metabolic by-products including urea, uric acid, and creatinine.
Native to Eastern and Southern Africa, this large antelope genus includes two species — one black, one blue — whose lineages diverged roughly a million years ago — what animal is it?
Wildebeest (VIL-), also called gnu (NOO or, NEW), are antelopes of the genus Connochaetes and native to Eastern and Southern Africa.
Also called the belly, this body region sits between the chest and pelvis and is known as the metasoma in arthropods — which body part?
Abdomen: Part of the body between the chest and pelvis. The area occupied by the abdomen is called the abdominal cavity.

Now built by Leonardo but originally developed jointly by an Italian and an American helicopter maker, this 15-seat medium twin-engine helicopter serves VIP transport, firefighting, and search-and-rescue roles — which aircraft?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
AgustaWestland AW139: Twin-engined, medium-lift helicopter manufactured by Leonardo.
Prized for its oil since Spanish and Portuguese traders carried it from South America to Europe in the 1600s, this citrus-scented herb also goes by 'beebrush' — what's its species name?
Aloysia citrodora: Species of plant. Aloysia citrodora, lemon verbena, is a species of flowering plant in the verbena family Verbenaceae, native to South America.
A towering 20th-century French mathematician known for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, he was a principal founder of the Bourbaki group. Who was he?
Named for a mythological weaver transformed into a spider, which eight-legged class of arthropods includes scorpions, ticks, and mites?
Arachnid: Class of arthropods. The term is derived from the Greek word ἀράχνη (aráchnē, 'spider'), from the myth of the hubristic human weaver Arachne, who was turned into a spider.

Steel-blue with wavy black markings on its back and silvery underneath, this shoaling fish thrives in the cooler waters of the Mediterranean, Black Sea, and northern ocean near Europe — which species?
Atlantic mackerel: Species of fish. The Atlantic mackerel's body is elongate, steel-blue marked with wavy black lines dorsally and silvery-white ventrally, its snout long and pointed.
Also called the lammergeier, this bird of prey is the only known vertebrate whose diet is 70 to 90 percent bone — which bird?
Bearded vulture: Species of bird. The bearded vulture (Gypaetus barbatus), also known as the lammergeier and ossifrage, is a very large bird of prey in the monotypic genus Gypaetus.

A natural cross between the pomelo and the wild mandarin, this Southeast Asian citrus is too sour to eat off the tree — but the Seville variety is exactly what British cooks prize for their breakfast preserve. What fruit is it?
Named in honor of physicist Satyendra Nath Bose and coined by Paul Dirac, this class of subatomic particle has integer spin and includes force carriers like gluons and the Higgs — what is it called?
Boson: Class of subatomic particle. In particle physics, a boson is a subatomic particle whose spin quantum number has an integer value (0, 1, 2,...).

Made up largely of the gluteus maximus — the largest muscle in the human body — these two rounded parts of the posterior pelvic region sit between the lower back and the perineum, and have long served as a target for corporal punishment?
Buttocks: Anatomical feature on the posterior of some primates.
Also known as meridian fennel, this biennial plant in the Apiaceae family is native to western Asia, Europe, and North Africa — what is it?
Caraway: Species of plant in the carrot family.

Also known as gotu kola or Indian pennywort, this herbaceous perennial from the Apiaceae family is eaten as a vegetable and used in traditional medicine across Africa, Asia, and the Pacific — what is it?
Centella asiatica: Species of flowering plant in the celery family Apiaceae.

Nicknamed for its spider-like look and also called airplane plant or hen and chicks, this houseplant is native to tropical Africa but can suffer 'burnt tips' from fluoride in tap water — which species?
Chlorophytum comosum: Species of flowering plant. It is native to tropical and Southern Africa but has become naturalized in other parts of the world, including Western Australia and Bangladesh.
A shrub-like bush of western South America with oval leaves and small red berries, its leaves are chewed or brewed as a mild stimulant and famously contain a notorious alkaloid — which plant is it?
Coca: Plant in the Erythroxylaceae family.
This miniature Belgian-French dog breed comes in two varieties named for a butterfly and a moth, based on whether their ears stand erect or hang down — which breed?
Continental Toy Spaniel: Belgian and French breed of dog. The Épagneul Nain Continental or Continental Toy Spaniel is a Belgian and French breed of dog of spaniel type and of miniature or toy size.
First flown in 1938 and built almost 14,000 strong at a factory in Buffalo, New York, this WWII fighter-bomber was known to British and Soviet pilots as the Tomahawk or Kittyhawk — which aircraft?
Curtiss P-40 Warhawk: American WWII fighter. The Curtiss P-40 Warhawk is an American single-engined, single-seat, all-metal fighter-bomber that first flew in 1938.
Spread by mosquitoes in tropical regions, this virus is often mild but can turn severe with bleeding, plummeting platelet counts, and dangerously low blood pressure — what is it?
A Canadian optical physicist at Waterloo, she shared the 2018 Nobel in Physics for the practical implementation of chirped pulse amplification — who is she?
Donna Strickland: Canadian physicist, engineer, and Nobel laureate.
Known as aubergine or brinjal elsewhere, this purple, spongy fruit in the nightshade family is technically a berry despite usually being cooked as a vegetable — what is it?
A German Jew who fled the Nazi regime, this social psychologist and democratic socialist helped found a psychoanalytic institute in New York and was linked to the Frankfurt School — who is he?
Once widespread during the Pleistocene and later reintroduced by humans to its ancient range, which hoofed mammal species is native to Turkey and possibly Italy, the Balkans, and Rhodes?
European fallow deer: Species of hooved mammal. The European fallow deer (Dama dama), also known as the common fallow deer or simply fallow deer, is a species of deer native to Eurasia.
Also known as the bodhi tree, this species is revered in four South Asian religions as the tree beneath which Buddha is said to have reached enlightenment — which species?
Ficus religiosa: Species of fig. Ficus religiosa or sacred fig is a species of fig native to the Indian subcontinent and Indochina that belongs to Moraceae, the fig or mulberry family.
Known online by the alias TiAMO, this Swede co-founded a notorious file-sharing site and stood trial for it in 2009, a saga captured in the documentary TPB AFK — who is he?

Germany's first professor of experimental physics is remembered both for the tree-like electrical discharge patterns named after him and for the witty posthumous notebooks he called "waste books" — who was he?
Georg Christoph Lichtenberg: German scientist and satirist (1742–1799)
This plant genus in the mallow family gives us cotton, humanity's primary natural fiber, with its name tracing to an Arabic word for a soft substance — which genus?
Gossypium: Genus of flowering plants in the mallow family Malvaceae.

Derived independently in the 1830s by two European researchers and later given theoretical backing by George Stokes, this law describes the pressure drop of laminar flow through a drinking straw or a hypodermic needle — what's it called?
Hagen–Poiseuille equation: Law describing the pressure drop in an incompressible and Newtonian fluid.
Nicknamed for its shaggy white spines that dangle over a centimeter long, this edible mushroom is commonly called lion's mane and is used in traditional Chinese medicine — which fungus?
Hericium erinaceus: Edible mushroom. Hericium erinaceus, commonly known as lion's mane, yamabushitake, bearded tooth fungus, or bearded hedgehog, is a species of tooth fungus.
This climbing, hemp-family plant's female cone-shaped flowers are used to flavor and preserve beer — what's the scientific name for hops?
Humulus lupulus: Species of flowering plant.
Formed by the merger of two hip flexor muscles that join at the femur's lesser trochanter, this is the body's strongest flexor of the hip — what is it called?
Iliopsoas: Joined psoas and iliacus muscles of the hip and thigh.
Native to Africa and Eurasia, this opportunistic canid can sustain a running pace of about 10 mph over long distances while hunting small mammals, birds, and reptiles — which animal?
A real estate magnate and Spanish–American War officer worth roughly $87 million, he was the richest passenger aboard the Titanic — and went down with it in 1912. Who was he?
John Jacob Astor IV: American businessman and Titanic passenger (1864–1912)
Derived from Greek words for 'movement' and 'study,' this scientific field examines biomechanics, motor control, and rehabilitation to understand how the human body moves — what field is this?
Kinesiology: Study of human body movement. Kinesiology addresses physiological, anatomical, biomechanical, pathological, neuropsychological principles and mechanisms of movement.
This genus of bacteria mainly infects amoebae but can cause a pneumonia-like illness in humans when it spreads via poorly maintained cooling towers — what genus is it?
Legionella: Pathogenic genus of Gram-negative bacteria.

This catch-all name covers over 7,000 squamate species on every continent but Antarctica — from finger-length geckos to the three-meter Komodo dragon, with a few 'legless' lineages thrown in. What is it?
Native to northeastern Australia and first commercially grown at scale in Hawaii during the 1880s, this is the only widely cultivated food plant indigenous to Australia — what nut is it?
Macadamia: Genus of plants indigenous to Australia.
Nicknamed the Red Planet for its orange-red appearance, this desert-like rocky world has a thin atmosphere made primarily of which gas?
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun, known as the Red Planet for its orange-red appearance. It is a desert-like rocky planet with a tenuous atmosphere that is primarily carbon dioxide.
This WWII German monoplane fighter formed the backbone of the Luftwaffe alongside the Focke-Wulf Fw 190, though Allied aircrew nicknamed it after its designer — which aircraft?

Messerschmitt Bf 109: German WWII fighter aircraft family. The Messerschmitt Bf 109 is a monoplane fighter aircraft that was designed and initially produced by the German aircraft manufacturer Bayerische Flugzeugwerke (BFW).
Awarded the 1976 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences, this University of Chicago economist championed monetarism over Keynesianism and mentored future laureates like Gary Becker — who is he?
Milton Friedman: American economist and statistician (1912–2006)
Named for a Tanzanian teenager who studied it scientifically in the 1960s, this puzzling phenomenon claims hot liquids can sometimes freeze faster than cold ones — what is it called?
Mpemba effect: Natural phenomenon that hot water freezes faster than cold.

Nicknamed the 'flesh-eating disease' even though the bacteria don't actually consume tissue — they release toxins that kill it instead — this fast-spreading infection often enters through a cut or burn. What condition is it?
Necrotizing fasciitis: Infection that results in the death of the body's soft tissue.
A subsonic flying wing with a crew of two to three, this nuclear-capable stealth aircraft was built to slip past sophisticated air defenses for the US Air Force — what is it?
Northrop B-2 Spirit: American heavy strategic bomber.
Named by analogy to how organs serve the body, what term describes a specialized, function-specific subunit within a biological cell?

Organelle: Specialized subunit within a cell. The name organelle comes from the idea that these structures are parts of cells, as organs are to the body, hence organelle, the suffix -elle being a diminutive.
Sold under the brand name Paxil, this SSRI antidepressant treats conditions from panic disorder to PTSD, and is also prescribed for premature ejaculation and menopausal hot flashes — what is it?
Paroxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It has also been used in the treatment of premature ejaculation, and hot flashes due to menopause.
Characterized by an enduring, inflexible pattern of behavior and thinking that deviates from social norms, this mental health classification impairs relationships and self-concept?
Personality disorder: Maladaptive patterns of behavior, cognition, and inner experience.
This scientific term covers walruses, sea lions, and true seals — fin-footed marine mammals whose closest living relatives are weasels and raccoons — what is the term?
Pinniped: Taxonomic group of semi-aquatic mammals.

A colorless salt that looks unnervingly like sugar but tastes acrid and bitter, this compound is mostly used in gold mining and electroplating — and just 200 to 300 milligrams will kill nearly any human. What is it?
Potassium cyanide: Chemical compound. It is a colorless salt, similar in appearance to sugar, that is highly soluble in water.

Also known as talk therapy, this practice uses regular personal interaction to help people change behavior and improve well-being, with effects research suggests often outlast those of medication — what is it called?
Psychotherapy: Clinically applied psychology for desired behavior change.

Distinguished from its smaller cousin mainly by size rather than any strict taxonomy, this long-tailed rodent genus numbers 56 known species, with 'kangaroo' and 'bandicoot' variants named for their appearance — which rodent?
Recognizable by its long, black-and-white ringed tail, this highly social Madagascar primate lives in troops of up to 30 and is dominated by females — which species?
Ring-tailed lemur: Species of mammal from Madagascar.
A Stanford physicist who joined NASA in 1978, she became the first American woman in space in 1983 — and, at 32, the youngest American to fly there. Who is she?
Sally Ride: American physicist and astronaut (1951–2012)
This long-term skin condition causes flaky, greasy patches on the scalp, face, and chest, and is called cradle cap when it appears on a baby's scalp — what is it?
Seborrhoeic dermatitis: Skin disease. Seborrhoeic dermatitis (also spelled seborrheic dermatitis in American English) is a long-term skin disorder.
The brightest star in Earth's night sky, this binary system in Canis Major pairs a bright main-sequence star with a faint white dwarf companion — which star?
Sirius: Brightest star in Earth's night sky. Its name is derived from the Greek word Σείριος (Latin script: Seirios; lit. 'glowing' or 'scorching').
Native to Central and Western Asia, this leafy green vegetable's high oxalate content can be reduced by blanching before eating — what is it?
Made by chlorinating ordinary table sugar and roughly 600 times sweeter than it, what is this sugar substitute also known by the E number E955?
This daisy-family weed's yellow flowers give way to fluffy silver-tufted seed heads nicknamed 'clocks' or 'blowballs,' whose seeds scatter on the wind — which plant, better known by its common name?
Taraxacum officinale: Flowering plant species known as dandelion.
This French aerospace engineer flew to the International Space Station twice, first as a 2016 European Space Agency flight engineer and again in 2021 aboard a SpaceX Crew Dragon — who is he?
Thomas Pesquet: French aerospace engineer, pilot, and astronaut.
Inside a ribosome, this cellular process reads messenger RNA three nucleotides at a time to build a chain of amino acids into protein — what is it called?
Translation (biology): Cellular process of protein synthesis. Translation is the process in biological cells in which proteins are produced using RNA molecules as templates.
RIKEN has been trying to synthesize this hypothetical element 119 since 2018 — the lightest element not yet made and the first of the eighth period. What is it?
Ununennium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 119 (Uue)

This Soviet cosmonaut commanded the first spaceflight to carry more than one crew member in 1964, then became the first human to die during a space mission when his parachute failed in 1967 — who was he?
Also called a slater or sow bug depending on region, this terrestrial crustacean is one of the few crustacean lineages to fully colonize dry land — what is it?
The symbol for chlorine is Cl. Chlorine is a chemical element; it has symbol Cl and atomic number 17.
The symbol for zirconium is Zr. Zirconium is a chemical element; it has symbol Zr and atomic number 40.
